Content:
In previous lessons, we explored converting larger customary units of length to smaller ones. In this lesson, we will learn how to convert smaller customary units of length to larger ones.

Content:
To convert between customary units of length, we use the following unit conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{yd} = 3 \,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
Let's get some practice at converting between different units of length.

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to determine how many yards are in [MATH: 34] feet.

Content:
To do this, we start with the unit conversion between yards and feet:
[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{yd} = 3 \,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
Since we are converting from feet to yards, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 3] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} \,\textrm{yd} = 1 \,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
The right-hand side reads [MATH: 1\,\textrm{ft},] and we want to know how many yards are in [MATH: \color{blue}34] feet. So, we multiply both sides of this equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{34}}.]

Content:
[MATH: 34 × (1)/(3)yd|= 34 × 1ft; (34)/(3)yd|= 34ft; (34 ÷ 3)yd|= 34ft; 11(1)/(3)yd|= 34ft]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 34\,\textrm{ft}] equals [MATH: 11\,\dfrac13\,\textrm{yd}.]

Content:
Sometimes we need to use long division when converting between different units. Let's see an example.

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{12} \,\textrm{ft} = 1 \,\textrm{in}]

We want to determine how many feet are in [MATH: 40] inches. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation [MATH: 40{:}]
